solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Prevent containers turning over

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning over says the word for containers is read from the bottom up, backwards

parts.note: pots are containers

explanation.surface: Someone tries to stop the bins from tipping over.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop something happening is to prevent it; the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Shoot up salad plant

definitions.meaning: to soar suddenly, as prices do
a peppery leaf also called arugula, eaten in salads

explanation.surface: A salad leaf that grows up fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Prices that soar are said to rocket, and rocket (arugula) is a peppery salad leaf.

clue.text: Uncultivated upland, space for climbing

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the word for space goes upwards, so it reads backwards

parts.note: room means space, as in no room to move

explanation.surface: Wild high country offers plenty of space for climbers.
explanation.definitionFit: A moor is open, wild high ground left unfarmed, typically covered in heather.

clue.text: He is second on it

parts.note: He is the chemical symbol for helium, element number 2 in the chart of the elements

explanation.surface: A man is runner-up on some list or ranking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' looks like a pronoun, but it is helium's symbol, and helium has atomic number 2.
explanation.definitionFit: Helium, symbol He, is the second element in the chemists' chart ordering elements by atomic number.

clue.text: Two pieces of meat for fast

indicators.note: Two asks for the word for a piece of meat to be written out twice

parts.note: a chop is a cut of meat, such as a pork chop

explanation.surface: A butcher's order of two cuts, perhaps for a fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' looks like a period without food, but it means quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation urging hurry means quickly, so it stands in for 'fast' as an adverb.

clue.text: Break, perhaps, in panel

parts.note: a jury is a panel deciding a case

explanation.surface: A panel takes a break, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks a break (fracture) as one example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A broken bone is one kind of bodily harm, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Red chief

definitions.meaning: a deep scarlet colour, as worn by senior churchmen
principal, most important, as in the four main compass points

explanation.surface: A communist leader, the red chief.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal red is a deep scarlet, and cardinal also means principal or fundamental.

clue.text: Couple with other siblings, initially in book

indicators.note: in says the earlier pieces go inside the word for book

parts.note: a tome is a large book

indicators.note: initially takes the first letters of other and siblings

explanation.surface: A couple feature in a book along with other brothers and sisters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives O and S, which follow W inside TOME.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of people together, such as partners, form a couple.

clue.text: Dye then natural, to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A dye that is then, to some degree, natural.
explanation.definitionFit: A reddish plant-based colouring used on hair and skin is a kind of dye.

clue.text: OK splits for each card game

indicators.note: splits means the letters OK break open the word for for each

parts.note: per means for each, as in per person

explanation.surface: Everyone agrees to split the stakes in each card game.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambling game played with cards, bluffing and betting is a card game.

clue.text: One quid to bag millions? Shut up!

indicators.note: to bag means to capture inside, so one and quid together hold the millions letter

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a quid is British slang for a pound sterling

explanation.surface: Someone hoping to turn a pound into millions is told to be quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shut up!' reads as a demand for silence, but means confine.
explanation.definitionFit: To lock up goods or animals in an enclosure is to confine them, as a pound holds stray dogs or cars.

clue.text: Related to change, modified

indicators.note: to change says the letters of related are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something connected with change has been modified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' turns RELATED into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something modified has been changed; the two past participles are synonyms.

clue.text: Pair of idiots at home — one's a killer!

indicators.note: Pair of asks for the word for an idiot twice

parts.note: an ass is a fool, an idiot
in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: Two fools at home, and one of them is a murderer!
explanation.definitionFit: An assassin murders a prominent figure, usually for money or politics.

clue.text: Journalist on the subject of drink

parts.note: re means concerning, about
porter is a dark beer

explanation.surface: A news writer files a story about drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A reporter gathers and writes news stories, so is a journalist.

clue.text: Music writer, terribly handy

indicators.note: terribly says the letters of handy are badly arranged

explanation.surface: A composer who is awfully useful.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Haydn was a classical Austrian composer, a writer of music.

clue.text: Reversal of roles for band

indicators.note: Reversal of says the word for roles is read backwards

parts.note: parts are roles played by actors

explanation.surface: Members of a music group swap roles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' suggests a music group but is a strip of material.
explanation.definitionFit: A strap is a narrow strip of leather or cloth, a band.

clue.text: Aren't, strangely, left payment for accommodation

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of aren't are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone protests that a lodging fee left behind is not right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' turns AREN'T into RENTA, then L is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Money paid to use a property or room is a rental.

clue.text: Super money

definitions.meaning: excellent, first-rate, as an exclamation of approval

explanation.surface: Wonderful cash!
explanation.definitionFit: Capital as an exclamation means excellent, and capital is also wealth used for investment.

clue.text: Knot tied originally on slant

indicators.note: originally takes the first letter of tied

parts.note: an angle is a slant or slope

explanation.surface: A knot was tied at a slant to begin with.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangle is a twisted, knotted mass, as of hair or string.

clue.text: Gran is struggling with a drink

indicators.note: struggling says the letters of gran is are jumbled

explanation.surface: Grandma is having trouble with a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' turns GRAN IS into SANGRI, then A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Sangria is a Spanish wine punch with fruit, so a drink.

clue.text: Note that may be passed back

definitions.note: a musical note lasting half a semibreve, the half note

indicators.note: may be passed back says the word reads the same from either end

parts.note: a musical note lasting half a semibreve, the half note

explanation.surface: A written message that can be handed back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' looks like a memo but is a musical note; the answer reads the same backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A minim is a half note in music, worth two crotchets.

clue.text: Publication, one for the wise men

parts.note: mag is short for magazine, a publication
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A magazine meant for the three wise men.
explanation.definitionFit: The Magi were the wise men from the East who visited the infant Jesus.

clue.text: Dressing briefly in uniform, a Yorkshireman

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the following words, across their breaks

explanation.surface: A Yorkshireman in uniform gets dressed quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressing briefly' suggests putting on clothes fast; it is a salad dressing shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayo is the informal shortening of mayonnaise, a dressing, hence 'briefly'.

clue.text: Price beyond one — furious

indicators.note: beyond places the price word after the word for one

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a rate is a price or charge

explanation.surface: Someone is furious at a price beyond them.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate means very angry, so it is a synonym of furious.

clue.text: Friend getting behind member, within the law

indicators.note: getting behind puts the friend word after the member word

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: A friend backs a member of parliament, all lawfully.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting lawfully means acting within the law.
